title: Create a theme and name it
prompt:
# Story 1: Create a theme and name it

- **Story**: XXX-create-theme
- **Created**: 2026-11-15
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open `stories`, press "New theme", type "Checkout flow" and Enter; press it again and Escape to see `new-theme`; open both and read
  the empty hint; reload the page and see both still there.

## Story

As a team member, I want to create a theme folder inside `stories` and give it a name, so that I have a place to gather the stories that
belong together.

## Acceptance tests

Creating

- [ ] **Given** the tree with the `stories` folder open, **When** the user presses "New theme" (the folder-with-a-plus button on the
  `stories` row), **Then** a folder `new-theme` shows inside `stories`, with the count 0, and its name is an edit field that has the focus
  and the whole text selected.
- [ ] **Given** the `stories` folder is closed, **When** the user presses "New theme", **Then** `stories` opens, and the new theme shows as
  above.
- [ ] **Given** a theme `new-theme` exists, **When** the user creates another, **Then** it is named `new-theme-2`, then `new-theme-3`.
- [ ] **Given** the `drivers`, `adrs` and `architectural-enablers` rows, **Then** none of them has a "New theme" button.

Naming it

- [ ] **Given** the name field of a new theme, **When** the user types "Checkout flow" and presses Enter, **Then** the folder is named
  `checkout-flow`.
- [ ] **Given** the name field, **When** the user leaves it (Tab or a click elsewhere) with a good name, **Then** the name is saved as with
  Enter.
- [ ] **Given** the name field of a new theme, **When** the user presses Escape, **Then** the theme stays, named `new-theme`.
- [ ] **Given** the rules of story 2 (spaces, accents, empty name, a digit first, a name taken), **Then** they apply to the name of a new
  theme too.

What the tree shows

- [ ] **Given** a theme with no story, **When** it is open, **Then** it shows "Empty. Drag a story folder here." in italics.
- [ ] **Given** themes and story folders outside themes, **Then** the themes come first, in alphabetical order, then the story folders
  outside any theme, by number.
- [ ] **Given** a theme, **Then** its row shows the count of the stories in it. The count of `stories` is the number of all stories, in
  themes or not.
- [ ] **Given** a project with themes but no story, **Then** `stories` shows its themes and not "No stories yet. Write a prompt.".
- [ ] **Given** a theme, **When** the user clicks it once, **Then** it opens or closes, like any folder.

Keeping it, and new stories

- [ ] **Given** themes, empty ones too, **When** the page is reloaded, **Then** the same themes are there.
- [ ] **Given** a project saved before themes existed, **When** it is opened, **Then** it has no theme, every story is outside any theme, and
  nothing in the stories needed a change.
- [ ] **Given** a story in a theme is open, **When** a new story is approved, **Then** the new story folder is in `stories`, outside any
  theme, and its number continues the count of all stories, in every theme (with 001 to 003 in themes, it is 004).

## Business rules and constraints

- **A theme name** is lower-case words joined by "-", with no accents, starting with a letter, of at most 40 characters, and different from
  every other theme in the project.
- **A new theme** is named `new-theme`, or `new-theme-<n>` with the first free number from 2.
- **A theme with no story is kept in the project** (the list of themes holds the empty ones too). It reaches the repository only with its
  first story, since Git keeps no empty folder (story 4).

## Out of scope

- Removing a theme, and what happens to its stories.
- Themes in `drivers`, `adrs` or `architectural-enablers`. Themes inside themes.
- A description, colour or icon of a theme. Reordering themes by hand.
- A filter or search by theme. Sending the theme to the model in a prompt.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `themes` (the list, empty ones too) to the builder data of a project, and read projects saved without it (no themes, every story
  outside any theme).
- [ ] Add the name rules: `themeSlug`, `checkThemeName` with its three messages, `nextThemeName`, `sortThemes`.
- [ ] Show the themes under `stories`: above the story folders outside themes, alphabetical, with the count, open and closed, and the
  empty hint.
- [ ] Add the "New theme" button on the `stories` row, which opens `stories`, creates the theme and opens its name field.
- [ ] Add the name field: focus and selection, Enter, leaving the field, Escape, and the message under it.
- [ ] Test the name rules, the new names and the order of the tree.


I also want to persist the theme in the database. it contains also the project id in the table (they are all tasks)
